This notebook relies heavily on: 

1. [Analyzing RNA-seq data with DESeq2](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html)

2. [RNA-Seq workflow: gene-level exploratory analysis and differential expression](https://f1000research.com/articles/4-1070/v2)

3. [Beginner’s guide to using the DESeq2 package](https://bioc.ism.ac.jp/packages/2.14/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/beginner.pdf)

4. [Count Regression](https://stats4nr.com/count-regression)

## Dummy Data Set

```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Number of genes
num_genes <- 1000

# Number of samples per condition
num_samples_per_condition <- 5

# Total number of samples
total_samples <- 2 * num_samples_per_condition

# Generate synthetic count data
count_data <- matrix(rpois(num_genes * total_samples, lambda = 10), 
                     nrow = num_genes, 
                     ncol = total_samples)

# Add column names for sample annotation
colnames(count_data) <- c(paste0("Condition1_Sample", 1:num_samples_per_condition),
                          paste0("Condition2_Sample", 1:num_samples_per_condition))

# Add row names for gene IDs
rownames(count_data) <- paste0("Gene", 1:num_genes)

# Show the first few rows of the count data
head(count_data)
```

```{r}
# Install and load DESeq2 package if not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("DESeq2")
}


# Create sample information data frame
sample_info <- data.frame(
  condition = factor(rep(c("Condition1", "Condition2"), each = num_samples_per_condition)),
  row.names = colnames(count_data)
)
```

```{r}
library(DESeq2)

# Create DESeqDataSet object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = count_data, 
                              colData = sample_info, 
                              design = ~ condition)

# Perform differential expression analysis
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Get differential expression results
res <- results(dds)

# Show the top differentially expressed genes
top_genes <- head(res[order(res$padj), ], 10)
top_genes
```

```{r}
# Install and load necessary packages if not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("gplots", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("gplots")
}
library(gplots)

# Extract normalized counts from DESeqDataSet object
normalized_counts <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)

# Subset normalized counts to include only the top differentially expressed genes
top_genes_ids <- rownames(top_genes)
normalized_counts_top <- normalized_counts[top_genes_ids, ]

# Create a heatmap
heatmap.2(as.matrix(normalized_counts_top), 
          scale = "row",  # Scale rows to z-scores
          trace = "none", # Remove grid lines
          margins = c(10, 15), # Increase margins for row and column dendrogram
          main = "Heatmap of Top Differentially Expressed Genes",
          Colv = FALSE, # Do not cluster columns
          dendrogram = "row", # Add row dendrogram
          key = TRUE, keysize = 0.85, key.title = "Z-score",
          density.info = "none", # Do not show density plot
          cexRow = 0.8, cexCol = 0.8, # Adjust font size
          labRow = FALSE) # Do not show row labels

```

## Real Data

```{r}
source("~/VHH/lib/utilities.R")
library(DESeq2)

# Function to calculate Levenshtein distance between two strings
calc_w_lev_dist <- function(str1, str2) {
  stringdist::stringdist(str1, str2, method = "lv", weight = c(0.99, 
                                                               0.99, 
                                                               0.01, 
                                                               0.01))
}


root_dir <- "~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/phylogenetic_dbs/translated_dbs/culled_databases/"
```

## Load

```{r}
files <- list()

files[["S14"]] <- "14_VecF1_R2_S14-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"

files[["S19"]] <- "19_VecF1_R3_S19-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"
files[["S20"]] <- "20_VecF2_R3_S20-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"

  files[[nm]] <- read.csv(paste(root_dir, files[[nm]], sep = ''), header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)
```



```{r}
library(pheatmap)

# select the 20 most differentially expressed genes
orderedRes <- res[order(res$log2FoldChange, decreasing = T),]

select <- row.names(orderedRes[1:20, ])

# transform the counts to log10
log10_normCounts <- log10(normalized_counts + 1)

# get the values for the selected genes
values <- log10_normCounts[ select, ]

pheatmap(values,
         scale = "none", 
         cluster_rows = FALSE, 
         cluster_cols = FALSE,
         fontsize_row = 8,
         annotation_names_col = FALSE,
         #gaps_col = c(3,6),
         display_numbers = TRUE,
         number_format = "%.2f",         
         height=12,
         width=6)
```




```{r}
# Install and load necessary packages
library(stringdist)

# Sample data frames
df1 <- data.frame(key = c("apple", "banana", "orange"), value1 = c(1, 2, 3))
df2 <- data.frame(key = c("apples", "bananas", "grape", "orange"), value2 = c(10, 20, 30, 40))


#The outer product of the arrays X and Y is the array A with dimension c(dim(X), dim(Y)) where element A[c(arrayindex.x, arrayindex.y)] = FUN(X[arrayindex.x], Y[arrayindex.y], ...).
distances <- outer(df1$key, df2$key, Vectorize(calc_wlev_dist))

# Find matching keys based on identical character lengths
matching_indices <- which(distances == 0, arr.ind = TRUE)

# Merge based on matching keys
merged_df <- merge(df1, df2, by.x = "key", by.y = "key", all = TRUE)

# Print merged data frame
print(merged_df)
```
